definition: AIVA (Artificial Intelligence Virtual Artist) is an electronic composer recognized by the SACEM.
details: AIVA (Artificial Intelligence Virtual Artist) is an electronic composer recognized by the SACEM.

explainer.lead: AIVA is an AI composing system that learned from classical music and went on to produce released albums and works performed by an orchestra. Its recognition by SACEM made it the first virtual composer recognized by a music society, connecting machine composition with established musical institutions.

tiers.eli5: AIVA is like a student who listens to a huge library of music by composers such as Bach, Beethoven, and Mozart, notices patterns, and then tries writing music of its own. It uses computer learning rather than human imagination. Its music has appeared on albums and has been played by a real orchestra.
tiers.practitioner: AIVA is applied to automatic music composition, with its commercial Music Engine generating pieces in styles including rock, pop, jazz, cinematic music, and Chinese music. Music Engine compositions are limited to three minutes, so it is aimed at short-form generation rather than unrestricted works. Its original specialization was classical and symphonic composition.
tiers.paperLevel: At a high level, AIVA implements C -> M: it detects regularities in a large corpus C of human-written classical music and generates new compositions M using deep learning and reinforcement learning architectures. The approach was initially directed at classical and symphonic music. Music Engine later broadened the output styles while limiting generated compositions to three minutes.

explainer.example: A concrete application is Music Engine generating a short modern cinematic composition of up to three minutes. Beyond digital generation, AIVA's compositions were also performed by the Avignon Symphonic Orchestra in April 2017.

usedIn.name: Music Engine
usedIn.detail: A commercial product offered since January 2019 that generates compositions of up to three minutes in several musical styles.

usedIn.name: Genesis
usedIn.detail: AIVA's first studio album, released in November 2016.

usedIn.name: Orchestral performance
usedIn.detail: The Avignon Symphonic Orchestra performed AIVA's compositions in April 2017.

flow: Read a large collection of classical works by human composers.
Apply deep learning and reinforcement learning to compose new music.
Deliver compositions through recordings, performances, or Music Engine.
explainer.origin: AIVA was created in February 2016 and specialized in classical and symphonic composition. It became the first virtual composer recognized by a music society, SACEM, and was presented at TED by Pierre Barreau.
explainer.lineage: AIVA's first studio album, Genesis, appeared in November 2016, followed by orchestral performances of its compositions in April 2017. Its second album, Among the Stars, was released in 2018, and the commercial Music Engine followed in January 2019.
explainer.whyItMatters: AIVA shows a path from learning patterns in an existing musical corpus to producing music for commercial products, albums, and live orchestral performance. Its SACEM recognition also brought AI composition into an established music-society framework.
